text:
RotatE (2019) weights sampled negatives using q_j=stopgrad[softmax(βn)_j], where higher scores indicate more plausible triples. Its official implementation explicitly calls `.detach()`: weights change between optimization steps, but gradients do not pass through their computation. β multiplies scores, so it acts as inverse temperature: larger β concentrates weight on harder negatives; β→0 gives uniform weights. Released configurations use β=1.0 or 0.5. With scores s=γ−distance, the loss is proportional to −log σ(p)−Σ_j q_j log σ(−n_j), with an additional factor 1/2 in code and optional example-frequency weighting. [Official implementation](https://github.com/DeepGraphLearning/KnowledgeGraphEmbedding/blob/master/codes/model.py), [configurations](https://github.com/DeepGraphLearning/KnowledgeGraphEmbedding/blob/master/best_config.sh).

The supplied masked-item candidate loss instead places weights inside a shared partition function: L=log(exp(p)+Σ_j w_j exp(n_j))−p. Algebraically, with detached weights and Z denoting that partition function, ∂L/∂n_j=w_j exp(n_j)/Z and ∂L/∂p=exp(p)/Z−1. RotatE’s corresponding gradients are q_jσ(n_j) and σ(p)−1, ignoring the overall factor. Thus candidate cross-entropy couples positive and negative scores through relative competition; RotatE applies separate binary logistic penalties. Candidate cross-entropy is invariant to a common score shift; RotatE’s logistic loss is not.

For 16 negatives, w_j=(1−α)+16α softmax(n)_j preserves total negative weight 16, interpolating between ordinary candidate cross-entropy and hard-negative weighting. Here α controls mixing, while softmax(n) fixes β=1; α is not RotatE’s temperature parameter. Detachment must be explicit—otherwise extra gradients flow through w. RotatE establishes prior art for detached self-adversarial weighting; the proposed distinction is its placement inside masked-item candidate cross-entropy and uniform/adversarial interpolation. That distinction alone does not establish novelty.
